j3_geometry_concentration_bias.finding: J3's flat per-hour base fuel favors concentrated short high-power bursts over smooth long low-power operation; planner already operates near the load+charge-cap ceiling, not the diesel max

solve_level_invariance.finding: J1,J_NC,J2,J3,u_diesel*,v_start* bit-identical to baseline in 100% of applied resolves

root_cause_mechanisms: cross-run reallocation: 330/2941 resolves actually INCREASED hour-0 charging due to whole-run weighted objective
closed-loop feedback depletion: postponed charging left lower battery reserve, forecast divergence then forced more diesel later
curtailment inefficiency: postponed charging shifted top-up toward solar ramp, causing more curtailment when solar arrived against a fuller battery
t1_campaign_evidence.decisive_conclusion: Diesel timing IS genuinely degenerate at the solve level (proven both theoretically and now empirically), but that degeneracy does NOT survive translation into the realized closed-loop trajectory under rolling MPC.
